title: Netflix AI Strategy for Competitive Advantage
subtitle: A conditional-go case for AI Script & Demand Prediction: reduce content-investment risk without automating creative judgement.
footer: Netflix AI Strategy · AITU · Group AIB-2402

layers.t: AI STRATEGY FOR COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE · AITU
A conditional-go recommendation for AI Script & Demand Prediction

slides.title: Original content is a *high-stakes* capital-allocation bet.
slides.lead: The strategic issue is not a lack of content. It is uncertain return on expensive, hit-driven creative investments while subscriber switching remains easy.

items.label: annual content spend — scale of exposure
greenlight made before audience response exists

blocks.t: Management question: can Netflix shift from spending more to selecting *better* without treating creativity as an automated decision?

slides.title: The defensible asset is not AI alone — it is *AI + proprietary behaviour data*.
slides.foot: Sources: Barney (1991); Gregory et al. (2021); Gomez-Uribe & Hunt (2015).

items.name: Netflix
items.sub: Data network effects + embedded ML operations

slides.out_label: Sustained advantage if adoption is responsible

slides.title: AI changes the basis of rivalry: from the *content arms race* to selection efficiency.
slides.foot: Sources: Deloitte (2024); Iansiti & Lakhani (2020); European Parliament (2024).

columns.t: Strategic implication: optimise for *retention-adjusted ROI*, not volume of titles.
Regulatory implication: explainability and creator safeguards are design requirements, not add-ons.

slides.title: Screen the full value chain — then fund the opportunity with the strongest moat.
slides.foot: Source: Group analysis; Barney (1991); Gomez-Uribe & Hunt (2015).

slides.title: AI Script & Demand Prediction: a *decision-support layer* before production spend.

items.t: Scripts, plot treatments and production assumptions.
NLP extracts pacing, narrative arcs, sentiment and genre signals; links them to historical audience behaviours.
Demand range, audience segments, geographic fit and a risk narrative — not an automatic yes/no.

slides.title: Netflix is data- and technology-ready; *operating readiness* is the bottleneck.
slides.lead: Scores are the group’s diagnostic assessment on a 1–5 maturity scale. The programme must close the red gaps before full integration.

blocks.t: Gate for scale-up: governance charter approved, redesigned human-in-the-loop workflow tested, and Creative Data Liaisons in place.

slides.title: The flywheel converts stronger decisions into a *data advantage that compounds*.

columns.t: Content executives, producers and ultimately subscribers.
Secure, proprietary viewing data and organisational routines.

slides.title: Trust is the constraint: design for *creative legitimacy*, not just model accuracy.
slides.lead: The initiative only creates value when creators, executives and regulators can understand its role and boundaries.
slides.foot: Sources: Raisch & Krakowski (2021); NIST (2023); OECD (2019); European Parliament (2024).

cards.title: Talent backlash
cards.t: Fear of displacement or algorithmic interference.
cards.cap: Mitigation: contractual human accountability; AI has no veto.

cards.title: Bias & homogenisation
cards.t: Historical data may favour familiar genres and markets.
cards.cap: Mitigation: audits; protected budget for non-AI projects.

cards.title: Script & data exposure
cards.t: Sensitive pre-release IP and behavioural data.
cards.cap: Mitigation: encryption, access controls and monitoring.

slides.title: Keep the creative executive in command; make the model *legible and challengeable*.
slides.foot: Sources: Raisch & Krakowski (2021); Dell’Acqua et al. (2023).

items.t: Budget approval never delegated to AI.
Scores show drivers, uncertainty and limitations.
Independent authority to pause unsafe uses.

slides.title: De-risk adoption in three deliberate phases — *learn before you scale*.
slides.lead: The 18-month path sequences technical validation, trust-building and workflow integration.

events.title: R&D + back-testing
events.t: Train on historical pitches; establish forecast baselines and audit criteria.

events.title: Shadow mode pilot
events.t: Score incoming pitches without changing executive decisions; compare predictions with outcomes.

events.title: Advisory integration
events.t: Make AI reports a mandatory input to pitch meetings — with human accountability.

events.title: Scale only with trust
events.t: Proceed only after governance, performance and creator-acceptance thresholds are met.

slides.title: Measure business value, model reliability and *organisational adoption* together.
slides.foot: Source: Group recommendation. Illustrative measurement logic, not a forecast.

items.t: Executive buy-in; AI-report usage; explanation challenge rate; audit completion.
Prediction variance between pre-production demand range and 28-day realised viewership.
Content ROI, retention and avoided downside from failed investments.

left.t: Go/no-go gate: advance only if accuracy improves *and* adoption and ethics controls meet threshold.

chart.cap: Illustrative trajectory: readiness rises while unmanaged risk must fall.

slides.title:
^^Conditional Go.^^
Build the predictor — *not an automated greenlight.*
slides.foot: Sources: Group analysis; Raisch & Krakowski (2021); NIST (2023).

takeaways.title: Fund the 18-month staged programme
takeaways.t: Start with back-testing and shadow mode; treat uncertainty as a feature to manage.

takeaways.title: Make governance a precondition
takeaways.t: Ethics Board, secure data controls, explainability and a formal appeal route.

takeaways.title: Protect human creative authority
takeaways.t: AI informs the conversation; executives retain greenlight and budget accountability.
